VZ (-10%) is down in sympathy with telecom peers after AT&T's Oct 21 report; its dividend (70.75c, payable Nov 2) is declared and the stock reports Q3 on Oct 26. Selling ahead of that print would crystallise a loss at a low point for no information gain. C (-12%) beat Q3 estimates on Oct 13 but fell on trading, credit-cost and yield worries, with analyst targets near $152 against a $120 mark, so this is a valuation-supported dip rather than a broken thesis. MO, BTI and PFE are up 8-11% and well inside their stops and take-profits. No stop is near its trigger, 32% cash is already ballast, and churn costs real basis points. Research was limited to a few web searches; the packet marks and those search results are the basis for this decision.
